description: Wire-level notification QA scenarios for a real Plasma/KWin session.

stage2.description: Stage 2 model assertions use the Krema QML surface or tst_notification_inbox; they do not replace v1 wire-level JSONL evidence.

qml_surface.heading: Notifications
qml_surface.sync_notice: Read and dismissed state is local to Krema; it is not synchronized with the app's server.

automation.wire_jsonl: not-required for model assertions; retain v1 wire evidence for the triggering notification

scenarios.title: Retain rich notification metadata
steps: Select a target desktop entry and keep Override desktop-entry from target enabled.
Set Summary and Body to unique run values, choose a non-default Urgency, set Timeout to 0, and enter default=Open and action1=Reply.
Press Send Notification and record the returned numeric notification ID.
In the Krema QML notification surface or QML harness, list notifications() and locate that ID.
Verify appName, desktopEntry, appIcon, summary, body, actions, hints, timeout, urgency, createdAt, and updatedAt match the sent payload; verify active is true and read/dismissed are false.
expected: The watcher payload is represented as one model row with the documented roles.
The QA app's sent record and Krema's model row share the same server ID.
No app-specific inbox state is inferred from the notification payload.
evidence: QML model view or test assertion showing all metadata roles

automation.wire_jsonl: triggering notification uses the v1 event contract

scenarios.title: Invoke a notification action through KDE
steps: Send a notification with default=Open and action1=Reply, using a timeout long enough to interact.
Locate the row by server ID in the Krema QML surface or QML harness and invoke action1 through invokeAction(id, action).

Capture the session-bus method call and confirm the destination is org.freedesktop.Notifications, the interface is org.kde.NotificationManager, the method is InvokeAction, and the arguments contain the same numeric ID and action key.
If Plasma emits ActionInvoked, record that independent observation; do not treat the method call alone as proof that the application handled the action.
expected: Stage 2 uses the official KDE InvokeAction method, not a private callback or a fabricated app API.
The model keeps the action label/key metadata available to QML.
Application handling remains an external observation.
evidence: D-Bus monitor or captured method call

automation.wire_jsonl: triggering notification and optional ActionInvoked use the v1 event contract

scenarios.title: Distinguish local read from local dismissal
steps: Send one persistent notification and locate its row by server ID.
Call markRead(id) from the QML surface or QML harness; verify read becomes true while dismissed and active remain unchanged.
Send a second persistent notification and call markDismissed(id); verify dismissed becomes true, read remains false, and the notification stays active until the server closes it.
Query notifications("", true) and verify active rows are returned, including a locally dismissed notification that has not been closed by the server.
Reset the QA app and close any remaining server notification IDs.
expected: Read and dismissed are distinct local model state.
markRead and markDismissed do not claim to update an application's server-side read cursor.
Dismissal clears the local unread contribution but does not close the server notification; active state changes only when a directed or broadcast close is received.

automation.wire_jsonl: triggering notifications and reset use the v1 event contract

scenarios.title: Replace one logical notification
steps: Send a persistent notification and record its server ID as oldId.
Set Replaces ID to oldId, change Summary and Body, and press Send Notification; record newId.
Query notifications() and inspect both lifecycle records.
Verify oldId has active=false and closeReason=replaced, while newId is active=true, has replacesId=oldId, and carries the replacement metadata.
Verify the app's active notification count increases by one logical row, not two.
expected: Replacement updates one active logical notification without double-counting the app badge.
The replaced record remains available for lifecycle inspection when retained by the model.
evidence: Dock badge count before and after replacement

automation.wire_jsonl: triggering notifications use the v1 event contract

scenarios.title: Retain directed and broadcast close reasons
steps: Send one persistent notification, then set Close ID to its ID and press CloseNotification. Verify the retained row reports active=false and closeReason=directed.

Send a second persistent notification and let it expire, or dismiss it from the Plasma notification UI. Verify the retained row reports active=false and closeReason=broadcast-expired or broadcast-dismissed, with the numeric broadcastReason retained.
If the server reports a different valid broadcast reason, record that value rather than rewriting it as directed.
expected: Directed CloseNotification and broadcast NotificationClosed remain distinguishable.
Broadcast close reasons update the model and do not remove retained lifecycle metadata.

automation.wire_jsonl: directed and broadcast close events use the v1 event contract

scenarios.title: Document the application-read boundary
controls: Read and dismissed state is local to Krema; it is not synchronized with the app's server.
steps: Send a notification whose body identifies this run and mark it read with markRead(id).
Verify the Krema row changes its local read role and that the dock-managed unread count follows existing badge behavior.
Inspect the QA app and D-Bus trace for the operation: no app-specific inbox read API, Slack/Telegram/Discord cursor, or server-side message-read acknowledgement is expected.
Record the result as local desktop notification state only.
expected: Krema can mark its retained notification record read locally.
The feature does not claim that the originating application marked a message read on its server.
A missing application acknowledgement is a documented limitation, not a failed Stage 2 operation.
evidence: D-Bus trace showing no app-specific read call

automation.wire_jsonl: triggering notification uses the v1 event contract

scenarios.title: freedesktop.org notification send, observe, and close
preconditions: A Plasma 6 Wayland session is running with its session D-Bus available.
The QA app is started with --scenario notifications-basic.
The notification server advertises the action or inline-reply capability when those observations are required.
steps: Select a target desktop entry and leave Override desktop-entry from target enabled.
Set Summary to QA fd.o notification, Body to a unique run marker, and Timeout to 0 or a value long enough to interact.
Enter actions default=Open and action1=Reply, then enable inline-reply when the server advertises inline replies.
Press Send Notification.
Confirm a sent JSONL record has dir=sent, mechanism=freedesktop-notifications, and the returned numeric notification ID.
Confirm the Notifications table shows the notification as active and a dir=observed Notify record is present through RegisterWatcher.
Activate Open or Reply in the real Plasma notification when available and confirm ActionInvoked or NotificationReplied is observed; record unsupported capabilities as a limitation, not a pass.
Set Close ID to the returned ID and press CloseNotification.
Confirm NotificationClosed is observed with reason=closed-by-call or the server's reported reason.
expected: The GUI distinguishes the outgoing Notify/CloseNotification calls from watcher and signal observations.
The event correlation remains stable from send through close.
No Krema implementation API is called by the QA app.
capture: QA app status panel before send

assertions: At least one sent event and one observed Notify event share the scenario correlation.
A NotificationClosed event follows the close request.

scenarios.title: Portal AddNotification, action, and removal
preconditions: The xdg-desktop-portal notification interface is available on the session bus.
The QA app is started with --scenario portal-notification.
steps: Press Auto to create a unique portal notification ID, or enter one that is unique for this run.
Set Title and Body to a unique run marker. Add a Default action or button if action observation is required.
Press AddNotification.
Confirm a sent JSONL record identifies the portal notification ID and includes the requested title, body, and actions without secrets.

If Plasma forwards the portal notification, activate its action and confirm the portal ActionInvoked observation. If it is not forwarded, record the forwarding limitation and retain the successful AddNotification observation.
Press RemoveNotification and confirm a sent reset/removal record for the same portal ID.
expected: The GUI visibly separates portal calls from portal ActionInvoked observations.
Portal forwarding into the fd.o notification server is environment-dependent and is never inferred from AddNotification alone.
The portal ID remains the correlation identifier even when no visual notification is rendered.
capture: Portal tab showing the generated ID
Forwarded notification and action, when available

assertions: AddNotification is recorded as sent.
RemoveNotification is recorded for the same ID.
ActionInvoked is required only when the portal presents an actionable notification.

scenarios.title: Unity LauncherEntry progress, count, and urgent state
preconditions: The target desktop entry is installed or otherwise visible to Krema.
The QA app is started with --scenario smart-launcher.
steps: Set Progress to 50% and leave Visible checked; press Send Progress.
Set Count to 3 and leave Visible checked; press Send Count.
Enable Urgent and press Send Urgent.
Confirm each Update signal is recorded as dir=sent with the target desktop entry and a shared correlation.
Observe the target dock item for progress, badge count, or urgent visual state. Record observed visual state only when it is actually visible in this Plasma/Krema session.
Send zero state: set Count to 0, clear Visible, set Progress visibility off, clear Urgent, and send each update.
expected: Unity LauncherEntry.Update is a signal with no protocol acknowledgement; sent and observed states remain distinct.
A missing badge or progress visualization is an environment/product observation, not evidence that the signal was not sent.
Reset returns all Unity fields to zero or not visible.
capture: SmartLauncher controls and sent event status
Target dock item with badge/progress/urgent state

assertions: Three Unity Update sent records are emitted.
Reset emits zero/not-visible Unity state records.

scenarios.title: SNI registration, properties, signals, and unregister
preconditions: The QA app is started with --scenario status-notifier-item.
steps: Set Id to a unique, non-empty value for this run; keep the service name and object path unchanged.
Press Register and confirm StatusNotifierItemRegistered is observed by the external SNI monitor.
Set Status to NeedsAttention and press NewStatus.
Change IconName and press NewIcon; change AttentionIcon or OverlayIcon and send the corresponding signal.
Set ToolTip title/body and press NewToolTip.
Confirm each outgoing property/signal is shown as sent and each watcher callback or monitor update is shown as observed.
Press Register again only to test re-registration; do not treat duplicate registration as a second item without an observed watcher event.
During reset set Status to Active, clear overlay/attention state, and unregister the item where the session permits it.
expected: The configurable SNI Id is the value advertised by the item, not a hard-coded label in the GUI.
SNI registration and watcher observations are distinct from visual presence in the Plasma tray.
The final reset state is Active and unregistered when supported by the watcher.
capture: External SNI Items table showing registration

assertions: Registration is observed with the configured Id/service.
At least one status or icon signal is observed by the SNI monitor.
Reset returns Status to Active and removes the tracked item where possible.

scenarios.title: KDE JobView request, updates, signals, and termination
preconditions: org.kde.kuiserver and JobViewServer are available on the session bus.
The QA app is started with --scenario jobs.
steps: Press Create Job (requestView).
Confirm the returned object path is shown as an active job and a sent requestView record is emitted.
Set Percent to 50 and press Set; set Info to a unique marker and press Set; set Total and Processed amounts and press Set.
Set a description field and destination URL, then toggle Suspended and confirm any request signal shown by the GUI.
Confirm job update calls are recorded as sent. Do not require a Krema notification: Jobs are not consumed by Krema's notification tracker.
Press Terminate Job and confirm the termination call and local inactive state.
expected: The returned JobView object path is the job correlation/id.
The GUI reports protocol sends and observed cancel/suspend/resume callbacks separately.
No Jobs-to-Krema forwarding is assumed; this limitation is visible in the QA status panel.
capture: Create Job result and object path
Signal log, if a callback occurs

assertions: requestView returns a tracked object path or reports unavailable service.
At least one JobView update is recorded as sent.
Termination is recorded and the job is no longer active.

scenarios.title: Inbox simulation, unread state, and badge synchronization
preconditions: The QA app is started with --scenario inbox-simulation.
The target desktop entry is selected.
steps: Create a channel with a unique name.
Send one message and confirm the Inbox list shows it as UNREAD with a server notification ID.
Confirm the resulting fd.o notification send and Unity/SNI badge synchronization are recorded as sent; observe any real dock badge or SNI attention state separately.
Select the message and press Mark Selected Read, then confirm the app sends CloseNotification and clears its simulated unread state.
Press Mark All Read if more messages were created, then delete the channel.
expected: Inbox unread/read state is local QA-app simulation state, not Krema application read state.
A message's server ID is used for fd.o close correlation.
The GUI explicitly labels the simulation limitation and does not claim that Krema read an inbox.
capture: Mark Selected Read and closed notification

assertions: A message is locally tracked with a server ID.
Read action closes the corresponding notification.
The run is reported as simulation-only for inbox read state.

scenarios.title: External watcher badge and local Settings inbox lifecycle
preconditions: A running Krema dock and a test window with a resolvable desktop entry share the private Appium session D-Bus.
The E2E test launches tests/notification/notify.py serve, which owns org.freedesktop.Notifications and forwards to Krema's /NotificationWatcher.
tests/notification/notify.py is executable with Python dbus bindings.
steps: Send two persistent notifications for the running test window and retain their numeric IDs.
Verify the matching Krema dock item exposes 2 notifications through its AT-SPI description.
Close the two IDs one at a time and verify the observable count changes to 1 and then clears.
Send two more persistent notifications, open Settings → Notifications, and verify both cards start Unread.
Use Mark read on one card and verify Read plus a reduced local unread count while the card remains active.
Use Dismiss on the other card and verify Dismissed plus a cleared local unread count while the card remains active.
Verify the inbox states are local to Krema and do not claim an application/server read acknowledgement; close all remaining IDs.
expected: An external Notify reaches Krema's running watcher and contributes to the dock badge count.
External CloseNotification updates the dock count without restarting Krema.
Read and Dismissed are distinct local model states.
The Settings inbox local-sync notice remains visible.
capture: Dock item AT-SPI description at counts 2, 1, and 0
Notifications settings cards before and after Mark read/Dismiss
limitations: Portal AddNotification forwarding into Plasma is optional and is not inferred here; use portal-notification for its explicit limitation result.
Jobs are sent to kuiserver and are not consumed as Krema notifications; use jobs for protocol-only coverage.
SNI, Unity, and DND compatibility are covered only by their separate scenarios when their external callback/property oracle is available.
Attention-animation pixels are intentionally outside this deterministic gate.

automation.assertion_source: Krema dock AT-SPI and Notifications settings AT-SPI
assertions: Two external notification IDs produce a 2 → 1 → 0 observable dock count.
Settings inbox transitions Unread → Read and Unread → Dismissed locally.
No server/application read synchronization is claimed.

scenarios.title: Do Not Disturb inhibition and observed property
preconditions: The fd.o notification server exposes Inhibit, UnInhibit, and the Inhibited property.
The QA app is started with --scenario dnd.
steps: Enter a unique app name and reason, then press Inhibit.
Confirm the returned cookie is listed and a dir=sent Inhibit record includes the cookie correlation.
Press Read Inhibited and confirm the observed property is true while the cookie is active.
Press UnInhibit Selected and then Read Inhibited again; confirm the cookie is removed and the observed property is false when no other inhibition remains.
If another application holds an inhibition, record that shared-session limitation instead of treating true as a failure.
expected: The DND GUI visibly reports the Inhibit/UnInhibit signatures and the observed Inhibited property.
Cookies are released in reset order, even when a call fails because the server already removed one.
The observed property reflects the whole session, not only this QA app's cookies.

assertions: An inhibition cookie is returned and tracked.
Read Inhibited observes true while this cookie is active.
The cookie is released during reset.

scenarios.title: Deterministic reset of every tracked protocol object
preconditions: At least one tracked object exists, or the reset is being used as a clean-session baseline.
steps: Press Reset All from the QA status panel.
Wait for the status panel to report reset completion and for reset JSONL records to be flushed.

Review the JSONL sequence in this order: close tracked fd.o numeric IDs; remove tracked portal IDs; send Unity zero/not-visible state; set SNI Active and unregister; terminate tracked jobs where possible; release DND cookies; clear local Inbox simulation state.
Confirm each attempted operation has a reset record with its correlation/id and either a success payload or a reason explaining an unavailable protocol.
Confirm the final status panel has no tracked notification IDs, portal IDs, jobs, cookies, unread inbox messages, or SNI attention state.
expected: Reset is deterministic and idempotent for objects owned by this QA app.
Reset never claims that portal forwarding, Jobs consumption, or inbox read state was observed.
Reset records contain no secrets or unrestricted message contents.
capture: Reset All button and pre-reset state

assertions: Every reset phase emits dir=reset records.
The documented order is preserved.
Reset completion is visible in the GUI.
